title: A spiritual friend
hook: the Buddha called good friendship the whole of the holy life (Samyutta Nikaya 45.2)
tomorrow: a town full of rival teachers. how do you pick one?

segments.voice: A friend in it: the desert kept Arsenius alone and Antony with his neighbor. Today, one kind of friend in particular, and a Pali word for them.
screen: `A FRIEND IN IT.` → `ONE KIND OF FRIEND.`

segments.voice: Plenty of closets hold a sweatshirt that used to be someone else's. Too big, a little faded, and still the first thing grabbed on a bad day. Friends leave things in our hands. Ananda, the monk who attended the Buddha, had been thinking about friends. One day he came to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said what he'd worked out: half of the holy life, venerable sir, is good friendship.
screen: `SOMEONE ELSE'S SWEATSHIRT.` → `ANANDA SITS DOWN.` → `HALF OF THE HOLY LIFE?`

segments.voice: It sounds generous. Half! The Buddha's answer, in the Samyutta Nikaya: not so, Ananda. Not so. Good friendship, good companionship, is the whole of the holy life. A monk who has a good friend can be expected to walk the whole noble eightfold path. Then he points to himself. Beings who are bound to be born, to grow old, to die, are set free, he says, by taking him as their good friend. The Pali word is kalyana mitta. Kalyana: good, lovely. Mitta: friend. So the teaching, in this sutta: the friend isn't a nice extra beside the real practice. With a good friend, the Buddha says, a monk can be expected to walk the whole path. That's why the Buddha can call himself the good friend. So a spiritual friend isn't just someone who agrees with you. In the sutta, it's someone whose company keeps you walking the path. Like the borrowed sweatshirt: something of them stays with you on the bad days. Ananda thought it was half. The Buddha said it was the whole of it.
screen: `NOT SO, ANANDA.` · `THE WHOLE OF THE HOLY LIFE.` · `KALYANA MITTA: THE GOOD FRIEND.` · `THE BUDDHA AS THE GOOD FRIEND.` · then, large: `THE WHOLE OF IT.`

segments.voice: Hold something a friend gave you, if it's near: a mug, a note, a bracelet, a book. Feel its weight, its edges, how warm or cool it is in your hands. For the rest of the sit, let that friend's name rest with the breath.
Kalyana mitta: Pali for a good friend on the path, the friend the Buddha called the whole of the holy life.
Your line: the whole of it. Not half, Ananda, the Buddha said: the whole. Day 1656, done.

screen: `DAY 1656 COUNTS.` → `OTHERS · 4 OF 10.` → `TOMORROW: A TOWN FULL OF RIVAL TEACHERS. HOW DO YOU PICK ONE?`

howItsDone: Buddhists speak of the kalyana mitta, the good friend on the path: a teacher, a fellow practitioner, the community. Some people name one spiritual friend whose company helps them keep going.

fork.setup: you're choosing between a fun friend who never talks about anything deep, and a quieter one who helps you keep going. which is the kalyana mitta?
options: the one whose company makes the path easier to walk.
the fun one, because a spiritual friend should keep things light.
neither; the Buddha said the path is walked alone.
fork.reveal: In Samyutta Nikaya 45.2, the Buddha calls good friendship the whole of the holy life: the path is walked with others.
